scope: OWL-derived dynamic AWDL election and synchronization-parent selection

experiments.name: dynamic-election-top-master-negative-control
experiments.endpointRole: distance-zero top master; initially mistaken for the intended distance-one receiver

experiments.name: rotated-endpoint-absent-control
experiments.endpointRole: previous distance-one AirDrop receiver address; absent before and during this run
experiments.interpretation: inconclusive endpoint test because the temporary address had rotated away

experiments.name: fresh-session-candidate
experiments.endpointSelection: new stable peer appearing after the user reopened the iPhone AirDrop share sheet

confirmed: The ESP tracked multiple live MIF peers, propagated top-master counter and metric, distinguished the immediate synchronization parent from the top master, and updated transmitted election state.
PSF observations refresh known peers rather than limiting freshness to sparse MIF frames.
The fresh-session run scheduled 14 probe groups with 1-2 microseconds measured lateness and radio-completed every MIF, Neighbor Solicitation, and Echo Request.
notConfirmed: No run in this slice produced a directed action, Neighbor Advertisement, Echo Reply, or admission event.
The intended distance-one iPhone address rotated before a valid post-election test, so distance-one admission remains unproven.
The five-second fixed-channel timeout was host-tested and built after the retained run but was not itself exercised in another active hardware run.
observations.fixedChannelFinding: OWL's two-second peer timeout is too short for an ESP32-S3 fixed on channel 6 when peers temporarily occupy advertised 5 GHz windows; the lab now uses five seconds while the reusable election core retains the upstream-compatible two-second default.
